factual_methodology.summary: Primary Treaty of Asunción Articles 21–22: express notice, denunciation instrument within 60 days, cessation of general membership rights and continuation of liberalisation obligations for two years. Mercosur official country page verifies Bolivia 2024 State Party/acquis transition and Venezuelan suspension. USTR verifies signed US–Argentina agreement 5 Feb 2026, not a formal Mercosur exit. EU Commission confirms Jan 17 signatures and provisional interim trade application 1 May; EFTA confirms Brazil/Iceland 1 Oct and scheduled Uruguay/Norway 1 Nov. Singapore and India government records distinguish staggered entry, launched negotiations and signed but not necessarily operative origin protocol.

source_vintage_and_cutoff.summary: Explicit 30 Oct 2026 São Paulo cutoff; 2023 bloc export destinations and 2025 Brazil-only shares kept separate from October 2026 tariff exception limits. EFTA 1 Nov entry is future at cutoff, EU interim application not final partnership ratification. Legal status, negotiation, signing and implementation are differentiated.

evidence_traceability.summary: 25 numbered bibliography entries and matching URL sequence in both languages. Verified major facts with original Argentina treaty, Mercosur membership/communiqué and tariff-exception POLCOM Decision 1/2025; MRE 2023 trade series ($684.5bn total, $379bn exports, $49bn intrabloc, 29/14/12% China/EU/US), IMF 2026 Brazil Article IV (~30% China and ~8% Mercosur), USTR, EC, EP, EFTA, Singapore MTI, India PIB and Reuters attribution. CRS 29 Oct version supported by indexed CRS record; some dynamic pages require future recheck.

research_depth.summary: Both exceed the research-report minimum by a wide margin after excluding fenced visuals and URL tokens; 29 ordered substantive chapters plus methodology/references, legal withdrawal and sectoral exposure, bargaining power, trade diversion, supply chains, institutional options and falsifiable scenarios. Added legal and 2026 agreement developments beyond prior structural Mercosur dossier.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: EN and PT-BR each contain three evidence tables (24 Markdown table rows), two quantitative charts (2023 29/14/12% export destinations and 2026 100/100/649/225 NCM exception caps), one causal flow, one qualitative regional map and one mindmap. Identical chart values and sequence; official MRE and POLCOM support numbers. Chart units/periods distinct; caps explicitly not actual utilization, and geographic map does not fabricate coordinates.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Institutional, neutral bilingual research with numbered in-body citation markers and all URLs in final reference section; no internal QA or product roadmap prose. Political alignments treated as attributed incentives, not proof of external control or formal withdrawal. No fabricated exit probability, GDP loss or precise counterfactual.

translation_parity.summary: Both full Markdown editions have 29 identically ordered numbered chapters, 25 identical numbered source URLs, equivalent legal withdrawal conditions, same two chart series and same visual types/order, policy statuses and caveats. English is canonical and Portuguese idiomatic.

novelty_against_corpus.summary: Compared 23 Sep 2026 canonical Mercosur structural report. This 30 Oct research adds 5 Feb US–Argentina signed deal, 2026 tariff exception Decision 1/2025 in force, Oct EFTA status, India/Singapore implementation, explicit Articles 21–22 exit analysis, trade-diversion mechanism, five conditional futures and operational tests rather than repeating only institutional history.

counterfactual_review.summary: Contrary interpretations include bilateral flexibility preserving membership, tariff liberalization improving input costs, common negotiation scale benefiting small members, and intra-bloc preference protecting some producers while diverting trade. Five scenarios carry observable tests rather than probabilities; exit cost is conditional on future agreements, input-output exposure and sectoral employment.

conflict_security_attribution.summary: Distinguishes state positions from verified legal acts and observed trade outcomes; does not attribute dissolution intent to US, China or EU without documents. Taiwan recognition and Venezuelan suspension are institutional constraints, not inferred conflict probabilities.

contrary_evidence: Common external negotiating scale may benefit smaller members; an intergovernmental bloc can endure ideological divergence without treaty denunciation.
Selective bilateral exceptions may make membership sustainable, while unbounded exceptions could undermine common origin and tariff rules.
Trade liberalisation may reduce input prices and raise competition but could disrupt cross-border automotive suppliers; no verified welfare counterfactual.
Signed US–Argentina bilateral agreement is not evidence of complete implementation or automatic Mercosur legal incompatibility.
limitations: Mercosur 2023 trade totals and Brazil-only 2025 export shares use different denominators and years; no pooled exposure inference.
National NCM exception maxima are authorized caps, not observed tariff-line utilization or proof of legal compatibility of a bilateral trade treaty.
EU interim trade application is provisional; EFTA/Singapore implementation is country-specific and date-dependent.
No verified formal Argentine treaty denunciation through 30 Oct cutoff; no defensible probability or numerical GDP-loss estimate.
Current source pages and third-party CRS mirror may be updated or restricted; verify original dated source versions before reusing claims.
Local full-repository Node tests unavailable; GitHub Actions build and strict-pending logs used, with candidate-specific independent checks.

contrary_evidence: An intergovernmental customs union can accommodate varying domestic ideologies without formal dissolution.

A signed bilateral trade agreement does not prove its complete implementation or legal incompatibility with Mercosur.
The EU interim trade agreement's provisional application is not the full partnership's final ratification.
